title: Selective Context token pruning causes severe PPL degradation
summary: Evaluated Selective Context with OPT-125m toy model. Medium context: PPL 2.90 → 18.01 (+521%). Long context: PPL 1.73 → 92.35 (+5236%). Importance-based compression preserves only beginning/end tokens, losing critical context. Approach abandoned.
root_cause: Token-level deletion disrupts sequence structure, causing poor predictions. Simple heuristics (preserve first/last 10%) lose too much context for long sequences.
fix_applied: 2026-04-23 04:15 - Documented findings, decided to pivot to KV cache compression methods.
validation_result: 2026-04-23 04:15 - Results recorded in RESEARCH_REPORT.md. Pivot to KV cache compression documented.

title: Q-Filters compression is a no-op in the current eval harness
description: Sliding-window sanity ablation (outputs/qfilters_sw_sanity/eval_results.json, PPL 3624.6413031372203) produced BIT-IDENTICAL PPL to full qfilters mode (outputs/qfilters_baseline/eval_results.json, PPL 3624.6413031372203). Root cause: layer.py wraps LlamaAttention.forward with a post-forward callback calling cache.compress_layer(layer_idx); this only affects SUBSEQUENT forwards. But evaluate_ppl creates a fresh QFiltersCache per chunk and issues one prefill — compression runs after, on state that is then discarded. Both modes silently degenerate to full attention. The '0.71x baseline' claim in UPDATELOG 2026-04-25 15:02 is invalid. Secondary bug: vanilla baseline (PPL 5102.22) used skip_chunks=40000 while pg19_chunks.npy has only 6441 chunks, so the baseline was run on an empty/wrapped slice — not apples-to-apples with the Q-Filters skip_chunks=200 run.
fix_sketch: Option A (cheap): change eval to feed each chunk as multiple sub-windows with cache carryover, so compressed state actually participates in the next sub-window's attention. Option B (faithful to paper): use needle-in-haystack / long-context benchmark where autoregressive decoding passes through the compression hook. Option C: move compression INSIDE the forward (pre-attention) so it gates the current chunk.
blocking: Further Q-Filters comparisons, kv_budget sweep, and the Llama-3.1 port are all blocked until the harness faithfully exercises compression.

summary: Fixed double-shift bug in 6 training/eval scripts flagged in researcher §8
notes: Each buggy script's dataset __getitem__ returned {input_ids:tokens[:-1], labels:tokens[1:]}. Combined with HF LlamaForCausalLM internal shift this caused a DOUBLE SHIFT (predicting 2 tokens ahead). Fix pattern matches scripts/eval_qfilters.py reference: pass tokens as both input_ids and labels unshifted; HF does the single correct shift. Also added the DOUBLE-SHIFT warning comment block per eval_qfilters.py:99-107. The other 11 scripts in the candidate set (benchmark_mac.py, eval_mac.py, eval_mag.py, eval_ppl_v3.py, test_selective_context.py, train_mac.py, train_mag.py, train_rmt_original.py, train_rmt_pg19.py, train_rmt_v3..v8.py, validate_smoke_loss.py) use MANUAL shift_logits/shift_labels over external logits without invoking HF's labels= path, so are not buggy. train_sparse_memory.py had TWO buggy __getitem__ (PreTokenizedDataset + JSONLTextDataset); both fixed. No hyperparameters/paths/seeds changed; seq_len-1 token accounting already compatible with new single-shift semantics.

title: Issue #110 exact-SVD fix PARTIAL — kv>=192 phase transition uncovered

diagnosis: Fix resolved sign-ambiguity noise at kv<=128 (kv=96/128 within +-10% of pre-fix). At kv>=192 a second mechanism drives PPL blow-up; pre-fix kv=192=123.56 was apparently a lucky draw rather than a representative point. title: Fix I: hidden_to_slot in optimizer but grad=None — dead computation path
description: After Fix I added hidden_to_slot to _mem_space_params(), trainable_with_grad went 128/192→128/224 (denominator +32 confirms param registered in optimizer). But numerator still 128: hidden_to_slot params have zero gradient (grad_norm=None, not small — literally None=no gradient). Conclusion: hidden_to_slot is NOT in the computation graph that produces the loss. Either (a) there is a detach() before hidden_to_slot is called, (b) hidden_to_slot output is not used downstream of the loss, or (c) hidden_to_slot is called on a tensor branch that is never used. Need to trace exact forward pass path of hidden_to_slot in layer.py/memory_bank.py.

evidence.fix_h_same_symptom: Fix H also showed hidden_to_slot.weight.grad_norm=None at same steps (before Fix I)

resolution: Root cause: slots.detach() at layer.py:499 in soft-proxy einsum + M_sel_hidden_hard.detach() at layer.py:506 in STE. Both detaches sever the READ-side gradient from loss → slots, so hidden_to_slot's gradient (via previous layer's write → scatter) has no upstream signal. Fix J-A: remove .detach() at line 499. See ops/research_notes/20260429_fix_j_proposal.md
